sentences.text: The Sequence Event Archive is the station's authoritative repository for time-stamped operational event evidence.
The Sequence Event Archive is known operationally as Orchard.
It preserves event records in their received form so later review does not depend on transient operator displays.
Each retained record includes its source identity, event time, archive receipt time, and available quality indications.
The archive preserves original event ordering and marks records whose time quality or sequence continuity is uncertain.
The Satellite Time Receiver supports station time alignment, and loss of its reference is treated as a condition affecting interpretation rather than a reason to discard evidence.
Events with corrected or estimated times remain distinguishable from records with valid time quality.
The Sequence Event Archive retains configuration and access history associated with archive administration.
The Station Supervisory Control System presents current operating indications separately from the long-term evidence held by the archive.
The Control Room Operator reviews archived event sequences to establish the order of alarms, status changes, and operator actions.
The Protection Relay Engineer compares event times and relay indications during disturbance analysis.
The Protection Relay Engineer uses the Relay Diagnostic Note during fault analysis.
The Engineering Workstation provides approved tools for searching, filtering, and exporting event records.
Review queries should be bounded by station, equipment identifier, and time interval to keep results reproducible.
Exported evidence retains original timestamps and quality flags, and any derived ordering is identified as an engineering interpretation.
Engineering conclusions are recorded separately from the preserved source evidence.
Access to archive functions is limited to authorized roles, and administrative changes are auditable.
The archive retains records under the station records schedule and applicable utility retention requirements.
Records selected for an investigation are protected from routine deletion until the hold is released by the responsible authority.
Archive health is checked for storage capacity, ingestion continuity, and recoverability.
Recovery testing verifies that retained records remain readable and that timestamps and quality indications survive restoration.
The station preserves an additional protected copy of essential event evidence in accordance with approved backup procedures.
The Station DC System produces a Battery Load Test Record for retention with station engineering records.
Juniper timestamps locally generated state changes for later correlation.
After the Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback, evidence from the completed work remains available for authorized engineering review.
